seo.title: Google Holiday 100: Lessons for Orange County Shops
seo.meta_description: Google's Holiday 100 shows 2026's trending gifts from Search data. What Orange County retailers should stock, describe and update before the holidays.

h1: Google Holiday 100: What Orange County Retailers Should Do Before the Holidays
answer: Google Holiday 100 is Google's 2026 gift guide built from Search trends, with jumps such as kitten heel sandals up 295% and adjustable roller skates up 180%. For Anaheim and Orange County retailers, it is a timely signal to update product pages, Google product data and in-store stock before holiday demand peaks.
key_takeaways: Google says there are over a billion shopping-related searches a day.
Searches for kitten heel sandals rose 295%.
Searches for adjustable roller skates rose 180%.
Utility jackets were searched more than ever.
Accurate product data now feeds AI shopping too.

sections.heading: What the Holiday 100 is
sections.body_html: Google's Holiday 100 is an annual gift guide based on the year's Search trends across tech, home, style, beauty and toys. Google says it sees over a billion shopping-related searches every day, and the guide highlights what people are actually looking for as the holidays approach.

sections.heading: Why local retailers should care
sections.body_html: Shoppers who search for a trending item often want it before a deadline, and many prefer to pick it up locally. If your Orange County shop stocks trending items but your website and Google product data do not say so, shoppers and AI shopping tools will send people elsewhere.

sections.heading: Step 1: match stock to demand
sections.body_html: Compare the Holiday 100 categories with what you sell. If you carry related products, make sure they are in stock, priced and visible, both in store and online.

sections.heading: Step 2: update product pages
sections.body_html: Describe trending products in plain language with the details shoppers ask about: sizes, materials, colors, care and what makes yours different. Use the words customers search, such as kitten heel sandals, naturally in titles and descriptions.

sections.heading: Step 3: keep Google's product data accurate
sections.body_html: Google's shopping features, including Universal Cart, which launched in the U.S. in October 2026, rely on accurate price and availability data. Check your Merchant Center feed and product structured data, and update stock levels frequently during the holidays.

sections.heading: Step 4: tell people you have it locally
sections.body_html: If you offer in-store pickup or local delivery around Anaheim and Orange County, say so on product pages and on your Business Profile. Shoppers in a hurry choose stores that can get it to them fast.

sections.heading: Step 5: publish a local gift guide
sections.body_html: A gift guide built from your real stock, with local touches such as gifts under a set price or gifts for visitors, gives shoppers and AI assistants something useful to recommend. Keep it honest: only include items you actually carry.

sections.heading: Holiday hours
sections.body_html: Update holiday hours on your Business Profile, website and listings well before the season. Wrong hours lose customers at exactly the wrong time.

sections.heading: Reviews in the busy season
sections.body_html: Ask every holiday customer for a review. Reviews that mention specific products and service help both Google and AI shopping tools describe your store.

sections.heading: What not to do
sections.body_html:
• Do not claim to stock items you do not carry.
  • Do not copy Google's list wholesale onto your site.
  • Do not let feed prices differ from your store.
  • Do not forget to remove sold-out items.

sections.heading: A worked example: a Costa Mesa boutique
sections.body_html: A Costa Mesa boutique notices utility jackets and kitten heels on Google's list and already stocks both. It rewrites the two product pages with sizes, materials and styling notes, checks that its Merchant Center feed shows the right price and stock, adds a line about same-day pickup and posts photos of the items on its Business Profile. Shoppers searching for those trends now have a reason to choose a local store.

sections.heading: Writing product descriptions that work
sections.body_html: Good descriptions answer the questions a shopper would ask a salesperson: what it is made of, how it fits, how to care for it, what it pairs with and why it makes a good gift. Avoid copying manufacturer text word for word; specific, original detail helps both shoppers and AI shopping tools understand your product.

sections.heading: Gift guides that earn links
sections.body_html: A local gift guide can earn links and mentions from neighborhood newsletters and community groups if it is genuinely useful, such as gifts from Orange County makers or gifts under a set price. Mentions from local sources help Google understand how well-known your store is.

sections.heading: Returns and holiday policies
sections.body_html: Holiday shoppers want to know about gift receipts, extended return windows and delivery cut-off dates. State them clearly on product pages and in your listings; clear policies remove a common reason shoppers hesitate.

sections.heading: After the holidays
sections.body_html: Keep trend pages updated rather than deleting them; many trends carry into the new year, and an established page with reviews is easier to rank again next season.

sections.heading: Using trends year round
sections.body_html: The Holiday 100 is one snapshot, but the habit it teaches is useful all year: watch what people search for, compare it with what you stock and update pages before demand peaks. Google Trends and your own Search Console data show the same signals for your products and your area.

sections.heading: Inventory and AI shopping
sections.body_html: AI shopping features can alert shoppers to price drops and restocks. Retailers that keep stock levels accurate in their feeds benefit; those whose feeds lag risk sending shoppers to items they cannot buy.

sections.heading: Photos that sell
sections.body_html: Use real photos of the products you stock, ideally in store or in use, alongside clean product shots. Post a selection to your Business Profile too, so local shoppers see what you carry before they visit.

sections.heading: Staff know the trends too
sections.body_html: Share the trends with your team so they can point shoppers to related products in store. A salesperson who can say we have those utility jackets in three colors turns a search trend into a sale.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Google's Holiday 100 shows what shoppers want this year. Orange County retailers should check stock, update product pages and product data, advertise local pickup and keep hours accurate before demand peaks.

faqs.a: Google's annual gift guide based on the year's Search trends.

faqs.q: How many shopping searches does Google see?
faqs.a: Google says over a billion shopping-related searches every day.

faqs.q: Which trends did Google highlight in 2026?
faqs.a: Examples include kitten heel sandals up 295% and adjustable roller skates up 180%.

faqs.q: How can a local store use the Holiday 100?
faqs.a: Check stock against the trends, update product pages and data, and promote local pickup.

faqs.q: Does Google's Universal Cart affect retailers?
faqs.a: It relies on accurate product data, so feeds and structured data matter more.

faqs.q: Should I copy the Holiday 100 list?
faqs.a: No. Build your own guide from products you actually stock.

faqs.q: When should I update holiday hours?
faqs.a: Well before the season, on your profile, website and listings.

faqs.q: Do reviews matter during the holidays?
faqs.a: Yes. Specific reviews help Google and AI tools describe your store.

faqs.q: Should small shops use Google Merchant Center?
faqs.a: Yes. It is how Google gets price and availability data for shopping features.

faqs.q: How early should I prepare for the holidays?
faqs.a: As early as possible; product data and pages need time to be processed and indexed.
